item.title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gke-kernel-network-bug/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794082671635.jpg"/><p>Google recently detailed how three interacting bugs across Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API connectivity failures, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Meta TLX, a Native GPU Compiler Extension Supporting Advanced Hardware Capabilities
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/meta-triton-tlx-gpu-compiler/en/headerimage/meta-java-kotlin-port-1795195032767.jpeg"/><p>Meta developed Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), designed to bridge the gap between high-level GPU programming abstractions and the low-level execution control required to fully exploit modern GPU architectures.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Uber Cuts Translation Cache Memory by up to 90% While Keeping P99 Latency Below 1 MS
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Uber redesigned its Go-based translation cache to reduce its initial memory footprint by more than 90% while maintaining a cache hit rate above 99.9% and p99 disk-backed cache miss latency below 100 microseconds. The hybrid architecture combines in-memory keys and frequently accessed values with disk-backed storage, reducing garbage-collection overhead and memory consumption.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-substrate-gvisor-cncf/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408775099.jpg"/><p>Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud‑to‑Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/tesco-enterprise-tech-transformation/en/mediumimage/JayeshBhayani-medium-1792654742095.jpg"/><p>Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco’s decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce.</p> <i>By Jayesh Bhayani</i>

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Future of Apache Iceberg
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/iceberg-v4-metadata/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795116071082.jpg"/><p>Apache Iceberg V4 proposes a redesign of table metadata to improve scalability and support more frequent writes, alongside new capabilities for data management and schema evolution. Daniel Weeks, co-creator of Apache Iceberg and member of technical staff at Databricks, presented a session at QCon San Francisco on the fourth version of the Apache Iceberg open table format specification.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Article: Building Reliability Into the Cloud: Observability as the Control Plane for Multi-Region Failover
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/observability-control-plane-failover/en/headerimage/header-1795002929606.jpg"/><p>Cloud SLAs promise uptime statistically, not absolutely. This article shows how to treat observability as a control plane that detects regional degradation, triggers automated failover, and confirms recovery rather than paging a human. Covers active-active architecture, DNS TTL pitfalls, composite Prometheus alerting, Route 53 weighted routing, and confirmation loops backed by a real S3 outage.</p> <i>By Saurabh Ahuja</i>

item.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-emulator-local-testing/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795086946449.jpg"/><p>AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

item.title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/healthy-code-AI-tokens/en/headerimage/header-1794837764807.jpg"/><p>Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

item.title: Presentation: RIIIR: Rewrite It In *Idiomatic* Rust (with AI)
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/rust-ai-symposium-agent-client-protocol/en/mediumimage/NikoMatsakis-medium-1793279155828.jpeg"/><p>Nicholas Matsakis shares why AI makes Rust the ideal choice for modern production systems, skipping steep adoption hurdles via compiler guardrails. He discusses Symposium - an open-source, agent-oriented toolchain from the Rust Foundation - and demonstrates how the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardizes agent-to-tool extensibility across diverse enterprise developer workflows.</p> <i>By Niko Matsakis</i>

item.title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads, reducing daily shuffle fetch failures from approximately 750 to 20. The deployment also lowered compute costs by 10%, improved application runtimes by 14%, and reduced shuffle costs per task by nearly 90% through dedicated storage, replication, and data-plane optimizations.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-privatelink-tunnel-endpoints/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794476042263.jpg"/><p>AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-cassandra-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794921404342.jpg"/><p>Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/quik-2-streaming/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794907611481.jpg"/><p>Qwik 2.0 Release Candidate, published on 1 October 2026, replaces v1's HTML comment markers with two script blocks that hold state and virtual node data. It adds experimental out-of-order streaming, async useComputed$, and cacheable route loaders. Qwik's benchmarks show v2 at 1.23x vanilla JavaScript, versus 2.59x for v1. A migration command is provided.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/datadog-ai-agent-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408423767.jpg"/><p>Datadog is extending its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, allowing engineering teams to compare AI agent versions against real production traffic rather than relying exclusively on predefined evaluation datasets.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Ten Years On, Google Updates the SRE Book for the AI Era
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-sre-book-ai-era/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794674690062.jpg"/><p>Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was published by O'Reilly Media. The update reframes SRE around modern cloud architectures, platform engineering and AI workloads, while retaining the discipline's original emphasis on applying software engineering to operations.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests without Jank
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-pull-requests-rebuild/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794747791339.jpg"/><p>GitHub engineers rebuilt the diff view in the Copilot app to handle a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and 400 inline comments. The design separates fixed-height code rows from variable-height comment blocks, which are measured in batches near the viewport. Performance is checked through CI budgets and automated app runs.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes Put Each EKS Pod in its Own MicroVM with One RuntimeClass Field
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-nitro-sandboxes-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794301940782.jpg"/><p>AWS has launched Nitro Sandboxes, running each opted-in EKS pod, ECS task or EC2 workload in its own Firecracker microVM with a separate kernel, enabled by one runtimeClassName field at no extra charge. A confidential mode adds attestation-gated key release. The documentation lists the trade-offs: no GPU passthrough, at most five sandboxes per vCPU, and half the compute on SMT instances.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/alpine-linux-openssh-sshhole/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794610199233.jpg"/><p>A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces Private Origins for Application Services
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cloudflare-private-origins/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793395278236.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently made Application Services for Private Origins generally available, allowing public traffic to reach applications hosted on private networks without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports. Private-to-private connectivity is not yet supported.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Node.js Brings Debounce, Throttle, and PKCS#12 Parsing into Core Modules
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/nodejs-debounce-throttle/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794593143949.jpg"/><p>Node.js 26.10.0 adds util.debounce() and util.throttle(), plus util.markPromiseAsHandled(), to the core library. It also introduces crypto.parsePKCS12() for reading .p12 and .pfx bundles, and extends the experimental Virtual File System to node:ffi. The additions reduce the need for some userland dependencies. Node.js 26 is now Active LTS.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Dropbox Shares How its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour across 200+ Web Surfaces
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dropbox-cookie-auditor/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794331089979.jpg"/><p>Dropbox engineers described a Playwright-based auditor that checks cookie consent behavior across more than 200 web surfaces. It runs three tests per page: US visitor, EU visitor, and Global Privacy Control signal. Cookie rules are kept outside the code. A companion tool finds live URLs. Weekly reports separate likely violations from false positives.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/effect-4-0-release/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794245718049.jpg"/><p>Effect 4.0, a TypeScript framework for typed errors and structured concurrency, was released on 30 September 2026 with a rewritten fiber runtime. The team reports a bundle size drop from 35.6 kB to 7.1 kB and about 6.4x higher throughput, though these figures are not independently verified. It also adds long-term support through September 2029.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
